title: Meet Daniel Hughes, the most interesting man in college football
description: A fascinating look into a fascinating Seminole newcomer.
fullText:
Levels of interest aren't exactly at their peak surrounding Florida State football entering the 2026 season.

And yet, the Seminoles have a new player in New Mexico transfer punter Daniel Hughes who has a compelling case for being the most interesting man in college football.

At 16, he dropped out of Year 10 (sophomore year of high school) in Australia, began a carpenter apprenticeship, was fully qualified by 19 and launched his own business.

So how did he end up as a college punter and internet content creator?

"I was not happy with what I was doing," Hughes said. "I was making a really good living, retired my mom. I was really comfortable. But money doesn't buy happiness, and I always want to be a professional athlete."

And so, he went back to secondary school (what high school is called in Australia), got his Year 12 pass (high school diploma) and got involved with ProKick Australia, even though he was much older than many of the other people in the program.

"About 25, 26, you sort of finish up your career sort of like towards 30," Hughes recalled. "I'd seen ProKick and I saw athletes that were over here that were half the athlete that I am. I was like, 'I can kick a ball, man.' So, I reached out to them."

After a few other stops, he's now 28 years old and using his final year of collegiate eligibility at Florida State.

When he was punting at his first American school, City College of San Francisco in the junior college ranks, he launched his social media account.

It grew mildly then and last season at New Mexico, but has really blossomed this offseason since joining the Seminoles. He has over 50 thousand followers on Instagram and over 25 thousand on TikTok.

There's football and punting galore on his accounts, but also day-in-the-life content, vlogs and various other forms of content.

Hughes says it's grown enough by now that he pretty much always gets recognized in public when he's out in Tallahassee, but that it's been an extremely positive experience.

"The community is great. I can't go to Publix or Whole Foods now without getting recognized. It's always really positive encounters, it's just 'How's the season going? How are you looking? I love your content, it brings such a positive light on the program and even some people's lives as well,'" Hughes said. "I get messages from people saying, 'Hey man, I was going through a really dark time and your content has like brought me into now going to the gym and just doing some really good things now.' So, in terms of the community stuff, it's always positive. But yeah, I can't really leave the house now without getting recognized."

Hughes' distinctive look certainly doesn't hurt his online presence. He's 6-foot-5, 219 pounds (down about 30 from when he arrived at FSU, he says) with much of his body covered in tattoos. While he's sporting long black hair in his FSU headshot, he's since dyed his hair a shade he calls blond but could certainly be construed as Targaryen grey.

Although he admits the content will be a bit slower for the next few months with football season upon us, he also believes his natural approach to being on camera has helped his viewership blossom.

"My content is very genuine and authentic," Hughes said. "There's no like, 'Oh my god, look at me. I'm going to fake this.' It's 'this is what I'm going through in life right now. How can I portray that to the Florida State fans and my community as well?'"

Now, to simply discuss his content is to overlook the fact that Hughes has established himself as a very strong punter in his own right.

Hughes' lone season at New Mexico under first-year head coach Jason Eck was a massive success, with the team jumping up five wins in 2024 to nine (tied for the most in program history since 1982) last fall.

He ranked 29th in FBS in average yards per punt (45.4) last season for the Lobos. In the much more important net yards per punt stat (average punt distance minus average punt return allowed), Hughes ranked seventh among players with 30-plus punts at 43.0 yards.

In his interview this past Thursday, he was quick to not take too much credit for that.

"(Net punting) is a unit statistic. It's not a Daniel Hughes or a punter statistic. So it was a unit statistic," Hughes said. "I just played my role in that stat."

New special teams coordinator Adam Scheier, who coached against Hughes last season when he was on UNLV's staff, felt more comfortable lauding him with praise and hyping up that net punting stat when asked about him that same day.

"I watched his stuff, and he's a very talented punter," Scheier said of Hughes. "Those guys joke all the time, right? I've got three things that are really important to me in life: my wife, my kids and net punt. So it will carry over. We will make an emphasis of attacking that unit as an opportunity to flip the field, because our job at the end of the day is to play great defense, and the way you do that is you move the ball as far down the field as you possibly can, give your defense as long a field to defend as possible, and I think it'll carry over."

Hughes, named to the Ray Guy Award watch list on Friday, did admit he's very confident in his ability to make all types of punts which could be required of him this season. He sees some similarities between the culture at New Mexico and what he's been around in Tallahassee, and is hopeful a similar leap up in success will be the product of that.

Until the games begin, Hughes is just prepping for that moment and relishing in where his truly unique journey has taken him.

"Every day, I wake up with a smile on my face. I get in my car at five in the morning, I'm so excited to come here. I was talking with Duce Robinson last week, and he was like, 'I'm so excited for you to see the warchant for the first time.' I think the first time when we come out of that tunnel, that's when I'd be like, I'm at Florida State."

title: Tennessee Titans Hidden Gems: 3 Secret Superstars on the 2026 roster
description: Can the 2026 Titans go from worst to first? Hidden Gems Tony Pollard, John Franklin-Myers, and Fernando Carmona Jr. would like to help that dream become reality.
fullText:
Nobody reading this site on a regular basis needs to be told that the Tennessee Titans' two straight 3-14 seasons are not good enough. That falls into the "Well, DUH" category for any NFL team.

So, instead of reliving the mistakes of years past, let's focus on how the Titans can rise out of the muck and become competitive again.

One reason for optimism is the development that rookie quarterback Cam Ward showed as the 2025 season went along. From Weeks 1-9, Ward completed 170 of 295 passes for 1,760 yards, five touchdowns, six interceptions, and a passer rating of 72.1. But starting in Week 10 through Week 18, Ward turned it around, completing 153 of 245 passes for 1,409 yards, 10 touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 90.0.

That was entirely legit. And new offensive coordinator Brian Daboll is excited about helping Ward take the next steps.

"He is a young professional," Daboll said of Ward in early May. "He wants to be great. He is instinctive. When we are just watching the tape, he is able to communicate the things that he sees, and why he did certain things, when we watch the tape from last year. When we are installing the new system to him, concepts and things like that, he is able to pick things up very quickly. It has been awesome to work with him."

New head coach Robert Saleh, one of the NFL's best defensive minds, does carry a 20-36 record as a head coach as baggage. But as that happened over four seasons with the New York Jets from 2021-2024, we'll give him a pass. We are not sure who could succeed with the Jets at this point.

And this Titans team is loaded with talent. Ward is ascending. First-round receiver Carnell Tate has the skills to be an alpha X-iso receiver, no matter what some may say.

Carnell Tate as your new alpha iso receiver. 

No need to overthink it. pic.twitter.com/mBnvr9ul2L

There could be at least five new starters on defense, if not more, and Saleh has to be excited about that — as we will detail, Saleh and general manager Mike Borgonzi have done a nice job of acquiring players who fit the new head coach's schematic preferences.

Can the 2026 Titans be like the 2025 New England Patriots, and jump from obscurity to the Super Bowl? That's a tall order, but stranger things have happened in the National Football League. For that to happen, of course, everybody on the roster will have to step up to unimaginable heights. The stars, yes, but also the guys whose names don't make a dent in a national sense.

To that end, I've identified three Hidden Gems for the 2026 Titans — one underrated veteran, one underrated free-agent signing, and one underrated draft pick.

When it comes to running backs, explosive plays are great, but consistency is just as crucial to ultimate success. The back who can upend defenses year after year without blips in performance will find himself respected as a franchise pillar.

So, let's note here that two NFL running backs have at least 1,000 rushing yards in each of the last four seasons: Derrick Henry and Tony Pollard.

Henry won't surprise you; El Tractorcito is on his way to the Pro Football Hall of Fame. But Pollard? The 2019 fourth-round pick of the Dallas Cowboys who signed a three-year, $21.75 million contract with the Titans in 2024, and doesn't make much noise on the national radar?

Well, yes. Consistency may be important, but it often avoids headlines. Especially on teams with stacked 3-14 records.

Regardless of how the nation views him (or doesn't), everybody in Tennessee should be pretty happy about Pollard. Last season, he ran the ball 242 times for 1,082 yards, five touchdowns, 39 forced missed tackles, and 10 runs of 15 or more yards.

The Titans' new head coach didn't take long to realize the value there.

"He's an unbelievable pro," Saleh said of Pollard over the summer. "Does everything the right way, brings a lot of juice and energy, he's a positive individual. I feel like he's in here all the time, working on his body, doing the things he needs to do to get himself ready, and then his practice habits are second to none and how deliberate he is. And I'm not just talking about live reps, but if you guys get a chance to watch a walkthrough today, I mean every single step he takes is deliberate in terms of the pad level, the hand placement, the eyes to make sure that he's executing at a high level and those are the reasons why he's so successful."

Tony Pollard of the @Titans is one of two NFL backs with at least 1,000 rushing yards in each of the last four seasons. Derrick Henry is the other. 

We all know how Henry does it. Here's how Pollard does it. pic.twitter.com/Om1p8hmx2D

The Titans also have veteran Tyjae Spears and rookie Nicholas Singleton on the depth chart, but there should be no doubt as to who's the leader in Brian Daboll's backfield.

One reason the Titans traded DI T'Vondre Sweat to the New York Jets for edge-rusher Jermaine Johnson II was Saleh's particular requirements for defensive linemen. Generally speaking, Saleh runs four-on-the-floor fronts without too much blitzing or stunting; it's on the guys on the line to get home. And it helps when Saleh has familiarity with the guys he's coaching as he does with Johnson, who was drafted by the Jets in 2022 when Saleh was head coach.

This is also why the Titans also signed defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers to a three-year, $63 million contract with $42 million guaranteed this offseason. Franklin-Myers also overlapped with Saleh, as he was part of the Jets' defense from 2020-2023, so Saleh knew exactly how good this particular Hidden Gem can be.

Last season with the Denver Broncos, Franklin-Myers collected eight sacks, 43 pressures, 11 solo tackles, 18 stops, and six tackles for loss. He was a stalwart presence on one of the NFL's best defensive lines, and he contributed as much as he benefited. Which is why I tagged him as one of the NFL's Secret Superstars of free agency.

"Our relationship, we have one of the best relationships in football, I would say," Franklin-Myers said of Saleh after the contract was official. "We kept in contact. When I'm down, he is going to shoot me a text, and he is going to pick me up. Relationships in football, they're so important. And I appreciate coach Saleh because I can always count on him. Whenever free agency started, it was like: 'If the opportunity ever came about and he was willing, and we set the financials straight, I would be more than willing.'

"And I am so happy to be back in this defense with him, for real."

Every great defensive line has at least one "glue guy" who holds it together under the radar. 

The @Broncos have John Franklin-Myers. pic.twitter.com/2oTBK7XwXK

Given Franklin-Myers' ability to disrupt anywhere on the line, and what that can do for those around him (including Jeffery "Hi, I'm the best defensive tackle in football" Simmons), the Titans should be just as happy.

So, the defensive line is pretty set. The offensive line, however…

The Titans raised a lot of eyebrows when they signed former Pittsburgh Steelers tackle Dan Moore Jr. to a four-year, $82 million contract with $50 million guaranteed after Moore allowed 12 sacks in 2024. I guess you could say that the eight sacks Moore allowed in 2025 technically constitutes "improvement," but still. Right tackle JC Latham, who also allowed eight sacks last season, is still figuring things out as he comes into his third NFL season. Outside of left guard Peter Skoronski, there are no sure things on this line, and that includes center Austin Schlottmann and right guard Cordell Volson.

Based on 2025 performance, one guy who could provide clarity is Arkansas guard Fernando Carmona Jr, selected with the 142nd overall pick in the fifth round. Carmona moved inside from left tackle last season, which was a good thing, because his 2024 tackle tape was pretty iffy. But as the Razorbacks' left guard last season, the 6'5", 316-pound Carmona allowed one sack, three quarterback hits, and 12 quarterback hurries in 469 pass-blocking reps, and his run-blocking was often above reproach.

"It was something [where Arkansas head coach] Sam Pittman came up to me, and [Arkansas offensive line coach Eric Mateos], and they're like, 'A lot of teams see you as an inside guy going into the league,' so I just trusted their word," Carmona said of the move inside after he was drafted. "They've produced a lot of linemen, especially Coach Pittman, so he had that vision for me and I trusted his vision. I learned it's a place that I like to be. I like being in that phone booth, and just getting after it, and just hitting people in the mouth, and being in those tight quarters. I feel like I really thrive in that area, and so moving inside this year was a lot of fun, and I'm looking forward to continuing to grow."

Carmona has said that he's either played or trained at all five offensive line spots, and the left guard position is obviously taken, so maybe he can push Volson for the right guard spot. The Titans also selected Indiana center Pat Coogan in the sixth round, so it's clear that the new administration understands the level of uncertainty regarding four members of this front five.

Based on the tape, I like Carmona's chances to mix things up.

The @Titans need more intelligent smashmouth on their offensive line. 

Rookie Fernando Carmona Jr. is here to help make that happen. pic.twitter.com/OflSq4Kh0h

title: Falcons – Broncos preseason recap: Not for the faint of heart
description: Atlanta now has a much clearer idea of what they need to work on, at least.
fullText:
Preseason games are fertile ground for overreactions, and we'll definitely see in the weeks ahead that we were too excited about some things (Jack Strand? Malcolm DeWalt IV?) and too down on others (Tua Tagovailoa? Mike Hughes?). There are small sample sizes, vanilla game plans, and matchups we'll never see in the regular season to consider. And despite all that, the broad contours can feel awfully truthful.

The Atlanta Falcons have to earn the trust of this fanbase after eight straight losing seasons and a lot of "this is going to be great oh no it's on fire" stretches over that span. Fighting the urge to declare this team the same old, same old is tough in light of history and what we saw Friday night. Because what we saw Friday night was ugly.

The Falcons lost 27-7. They had a couple of serious drives, one which ended with a Jack Strand touchdown plunge and the other which ended in a tipped Cooper Rush pass that was returned 98 yards for a Denver score. They looked like a much lesser team compared to the Broncos, who are an AFC Super Bowl hopeful in 2026.

Whatever string these players are on the depth charts for either team, the Broncos players just seem bigger/faster/stronger. 

Breaking tackles, getting open, winning the LOS.

How much stock should we put in that? On one hand, without Jawaan Taylor or Jake Matthews or Bijan Robinson, the offense is obviously going to be lesser. On the other, 28 yards on two drives for offensive starters is the kind of result that sees you fall behind by a touchdown or more in a regular season game. Getting burnt to a crisp by Jarrett Stidham is a bad result no matter how many starters are out or how little effort you're putting into complexity and pressure, and no matter how talented Denver's offense may be around Stidham. When you're talking about special teams being far more impressive, you are talking about a team that has not played well, and we all fear that this team is going to get to the regular season and not play well.

I think this franchise is too hellbent on digging out of the past to be nonchalant about this result, unlike the past three regimes when preseason went poorly. I have to question whether their drive to get better will translate to better outcomes, because there's only so much time and so much talent to work this all out before the opener. But I do ultimately have to cite the unpredictability and sheer weirdness of preseason, where the talent levels on the field are wildly uneven and coaches are putting in varying levels of effort in terms of their creative play calling and effort, in saying this result should not cause us to hit the panic button on the 2026 Falcons season. It should, instead, simply make us wary, which is something we already should be given the way this franchise has let us down again and again.

Instead of indulging doom, let's be sober about what went wrong and bright about what went right, even if those scales are wildly unbalanced. On to the full recap.

Jack Strand nearly threw an interception, but he followed that up with a zippy deep ball to Vinny Anthony that missed by a little and then led a touchdown drive that featured a couple of nice short passes to Josh Simon and a sneak for a score. On a night where Cooper Rush looked ghastly, Strand simply seeming far more competent than a UDFA quarterback has any right to likely helped him.

Someone has to take control of this RB3 battle, and I think Tyler Goodson is well on his way. I saw a player who showed quality hands when called upon, but more than that showed strong burst and balance as a runner, especially on a long rumble where he stiff armed, absorbed a lot of contact, and stayed on his feet. Given his versatility—he can block, he can catch, and he plays special teams—Goodson just needs to keep it going to take the lead in this particular competition.

Tua leaned on Kyle Pitts, who looks lean, sure-handed, and ready to go. Watching Pitts reel in his targets early on and make something of them when the rest of the offense was silent is a good sign for his 2026 season. If Tua's going to look to the middle of the field for a big target who can catch, Pitts is going to rack them up.

Vinny Anthony has been a reliable target at training camp, but he caught my attention with his returns in this one. Anthony looked fast and confident and picked up a couple of really nice kick returns, which can only help his chances of sticking around. The fact that Rush and Strand missed him multiple times does not take anything away from his ability as a receiver, which I think is evident.

Chris Blair had maybe the single most impressive offensive play of the night, a leaping grab where he took a big hit and barely saw the ball jostled. Blair has been reliable every summer thus far and should, in my opinion, be ticketed for a practice squad spot at worst.

Both Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins Jr. looked like the kind of aggressive, capable linebackers the Falcons sorely need out there. The team trusting Daniels with the green dot is huge for a mid round rookie, but I've thought since he was drafted that Daniels has the requisite smarts and physicality to seize a major role on this defense. Perkins, meanwhile, looks like a ball of fire willing and able to fly to the ball no matter what the offense is doing, something that could make him chaotic fun whenever he gets into games in 2026. It's very early, but the future looks bright for this group.

Josh Woods is going to make this team based on his special teams ability, but the better he looks on defense, the better his chances are. I thought his second half performance was once again strong, as he put up a handful of really good tackles and flew to the ball.

Darnay Holmes had one coverage lapse by my count, but otherwise looked good playing quite a bit in the first half. He was aggressive getting to the ball and showed quality instincts, qualities he had with the Raiders that were not on display consistently. He's spent this summer pushing for a roster spot and may well get it.

I thought DeMarcco Hellams, who limped off the field but is hopefully okay, delivered a customarily strong summer night with his tackling. He's a very logical third safety with Sydney Brown (who also had his moments) filling in a hybrid corner/safety role, and I hope he can lock it up.

Your special teams contributors hoping to make it based on preseason performances on defense had their moments in this one. JD Bertrand punched out a ball that Jammie Robinson lunged on, giving Atlanta a shot at its first score of the game. Bertrand faces an uphill battle to make this roster while Robinson seems like a strong bet, and plays like that help both.

Jake Bailey showed off a nice leg, averaging 50ish yards on his all-too-frequent boots in this one. The veteran punter is replacing Bradley Pinion, who had been reliable for Atlanta over the past few seasons, and looks like he'll be a good pickup. If the team wants to keep an alternate option around, Matthew Hayball also delivered some impressive punts of his own.

Finally but certainly not least, Malcolm DeWalt IV looks like he might turn into something sooner than later. He looked impressive as a gunner on special teams and made one of the best plays of the night on an underthrown Sam Ehlinger deep ball, reading it perfectly and leaping to snatch it away from Denver's receiver for an interception in the fourth quarter. If you can play special teams at a high level and make plays like that, you have a future in this league, even if the pick was (unfairly, cruelly) overturned.

The starting offense looked bad. There was no Bijan Robinson and Jake Matthews exited on the second drive with an injury, but Tua Tagovailoa looked a bit skittish under pressure before the pressure started coming in so quickly he had absolutely no shot. We did see him heavily target Kyle Pitts, who will likely be his absolute favorite receiving option over the middle early in 2026, as I noted above. Seeing a bit more from this offense against a very good Denver defense would've done much to set my mind at ease, even if I know Stefanski vowed there would be few wrinkles in what the team did this preseason. Tua was not, for the record, satisfied with the performance.

If Tua looked a bit shaky, Cooper Rush started things off even more poorly. His first pass was a shaky one that missed badly, and his second was a duck that was intercepted by Riley Moss. He would settle in after that, leading the Falcons inside the red zone late in the second quarter, but then threw an ill-advised ball that was tipped into the air, intercepted, and returned 98 yards for a touchdown. That's not going to help your case for QB3, to say the least.

The offensive line was a cause for concern much of the evening, with things really only settling when Denver and Atlanta mostly had their deep reserves in. Having Mike Jerrell and Ethan Onianwa at left and right tackle respectively led to some hilariously humiliating reps where Tua could not have thrown the ball if he had the reflexes of a particularly caffeinated cat, which is part of the process for a rookie like Onianwa and mighty concerning for a more veteran player like Jerrell. We'll need to see some gradual improvement, at minimum, plus the return of Jawaan Taylor to feel better about this line and this line depth heading into the season.

The lack of pass rush was not shocking, but was still rough. There were good reps from James Pearce Jr., Zach Harrison, Brandon Dorlus, and a handful of others along the way, but by and large the lack of pressure on Jarrett Stidham and Sam Ehlinger led to both players being able to stand in the pocket and rip passes and/or take off running for respectable gains. I expect better from this front seven in the regular season—my faith in Harrison, Dorlus, and defensive line coach Nate Ollie remains strong—but no minds were set at ease last night.

Chris Williams had an uneven night, but he was one of the few Falcons defensive linemen not named Brandon Dorlus that actually generated some pressure. What was most disappointing overall about the night for Atlanta's line was that they couldn't seem to generate any real push on a consistent basis, which led to some of Stidham's most embarrassing passes and many long runs from Denver's deep stables of backs.

Mike Hughes was on the wrong end of two Jarrett Stidham passes in the first quarter, the first one a 13 yard floater for a first down on the game's first offensive play and the second a 40 yard bomb where Hughes got stuck behind Courtland Sutton and couldn't impact the play. It's preseason, but I don't think Hughes is locked into a starting job and can't look that shaky in coverage all preseason and keep one.

Rough night for Cobee Bryant, who didn't play poorly in coverage but was flagged (by my count) three separate times for holding and pass interference working with the third-string defense late in this game. Despite the evident talent he showed at times last year, that number of flags if going to earn negative attention from this coaching staff, even if the DPI call was pretty bogus.

I'm singling out players chiefly because of camp battles, but I do think it's worth noting that the first string and even second string defense struggled mightily to rush the passer, stop the run, and work effectively in coverage with a handful of exceptions. I'm sure Jeff Ulbrich had plenty to say.

I'll go with DeWalt, who probably did more for his stock than any other player on the field Friday night. Isn't that what preseason is all about?

We're just about a month away from the regular season, and the Falcons look like they need every second of that time to get work on improving.

The Colts. Atlanta will be heading to Indianapolis for joint practices and then a preseason game, and we can expect to see very few starters in that game given the emphasis being placed on practice.

title: Aston Martin’s 2027 Aramco Funding Frozen Amid Middle East Conflict, Insider Reports
description: A major geopolitical crisis is reportedly spilling over into the Formula 1 paddock, threatening to blow a massive hole in Aston Martin’s long-term financial and technical strategy. According to prominent F1 business insider Marc Limacher, Saudi Arabia has frozen its…
fullText:
A major geopolitical crisis is reportedly spilling over into the Formula 1 paddock, threatening to blow a massive hole in Aston Martin's long-term financial and technical strategy.

According to prominent F1 business insider Marc Limacher, Saudi Arabia has frozen its massive title sponsorship with the Silverstone-based team for the 2027 season due to escalating conflicts in the Middle East.

The news broke via a social media post from Limacher, a well-known F1 financial journalist and author of the specialized Business Book GP.

Limacher's post dropped a massive bombshell on the team's financial outlook, claiming that "Saudi Arabia, after several months of discussions, has frozen the sponsorship of the Aston Martin #F1 team for 2027."

The timing of the freeze is especially shocking given the team's previously upward financial trajectory. Aston Martin has been investing heavily in its new AMR Technology Campus, and corporate backing was expected to grow. "Riyadh was supposed to increase its Aramco sponsorship and bring a third sponsor to the team's portfolio," Limacher noted in the post.

The sudden financial reversal appears to be entirely out of executive chairman Lawrence Stroll's control.

According to Limacher, "The war in Iran is delaying the project." With the regional conflict demanding massive economic, defensive, and strategic shifts from the Saudi government, extravagant international marketing expenditures—like global motorsport sponsorships—appear to be taking an immediate back seat.

If Aramco's funding is indeed frozen for 2027, it could spell disaster for Aston Martin's most critical transition.

In late 2023, Aramco signed a highly publicized contract extension to remain the exclusive title sponsor of the team through the 2028 season. However, Aramco's involvement isn't merely financial; it is a foundational pillar of the team's on-track performance.

Starting in 2026, Aston Martin became the official works team for Honda power units. As part of that strategic alliance, Aramco was specifically tasked with developing the 100% sustainable advanced fuels and specialized lubricants required under the FIA's new 2026 engine regulations.

If Saudi Arabia pulls its financial and technical support from the project just one year into the new Honda partnership, Aston Martin could find itself scrambling for both a title sponsor and a cutting-edge fuel supplier right in the middle of a championship window.

Neither Aston Martin nor Aramco has issued an official statement regarding the reported freeze, but the paddock will undoubtedly be watching the Middle East closely as the situation develops.

title: How to watch Seahawks vs. Raiders even if you live outside Seattle

On Saturday, Aug. 15 at 5 pm PT, with pre-game coverage on KING-5 starting at 4:30 pm PT.

If you have access to any of these channels, you can watch the Seahawks!

title: Saturday BP: What are you still watching for?
description: What’s keeping your TV turned on?
fullText:
The San Francisco Giants have 40 games remaining. In all likelihood, they're going to lose most of those games. They've been a bad team all year, and then they went and traded a significant chunk of their talent at the deadline (as they should have, I might add). As such, the Giants have gone a meek 3-7 since trading Luis Arráez, Robbie Ray, Heliot Ramos, Tyler Mahle, Erik Miller, and Caleb Kilian, despite seven of those games being at home.

Over the next 40 games, the Giants are likely to pitch poorly, hit poorly, and defend poorly. They might even find a few more ways to embarrass themselves beyond the standard being bad at baseball stuff.

Yet during Friday's feckless loss to the equally miserable Colorado Rockies, there was a moment that got me thinking. It came a few seconds after Bryce Eldridge absolutely annihilated a baseball — off a lefty, no less — for one of the most mesmerizing home runs of the season. Here, let's watch it together.

After that home run, I checked in on the Giants chatter on Bluesky, and I saw a common refrain. Different users were posting different iterations of the same thought: this is why I'll keep watching the Giants this year.

Eldridge mashing dingers and (hopefully) further developing into a face of the franchise is one of the main reasons to watch the Giants, but it's not the only one.

There will be milestones, such as on Friday, when Trent Harris recorded his first career strikeout; likely later today we'll see Turner Hill make his MLB debut. It will be the 10th MLB debut this season for a Giants player, and almost surely not the last.

There will be battles for future roles. Can Hill, Jonah Cox, or Drew Gilbert make a clear case to be the starting center fielder next year? Can Victor Bericoto (or perhaps Parks Harber, Bo Davidson, or Scott Bandura) emerge as the everyday left fielder? Will Blade Tidwell or Carson Whisenhunt, who have cemented their spots as starters in 2026, cement those same roles for 2027? Can anyone pitch in relief?

There will be fun moments and highlight plays and, above all else, some final games for Mike Krukow to broadcast.

So what — if anything — is keeping you watching?

title: 6 NBA teams screwed over by the schedule release
description: The idea of playing a balanced schedule is a rarity in American professional sports. An NFL team that finishes in first place in their division one year draws other first-place teams on the schedule the next year. NHL calendars lean heavily on divisional matchups and regional rivalries. MLB moved to a more balanced schedule in […]
fullText:
The idea of playing a balanced schedule is a rarity in American professional sports. An NFL team that finishes in first place in their division one year draws other first-place teams on the schedule the next year. NHL calendars lean heavily on divisional matchups and regional rivalries. MLB moved to a more balanced schedule in 2023, reducing the number of division games and increasing interleague play to even things out.

The NBA does not play a balanced schedule, but the biggest factor in an individual team's success often feels like it has more to do with the travel arrangements than who they're playing on a particular night. Trimming the NBA's 82-game regular season schedule always felt like a silver bullet for many of the league's most pressing problems. Until that happens, teams are still jetting around the country every night to try to sell out as many arenas as possible.

The 2026-27 NBA schedule came out this week. Read our take on the league's 10 biggest rivalries for the upcoming season. With a little help from Shamit Dua's NBA Schedule Dash Board, these are the teams who got hit the hardest by the schedule makers this year.

The Celtics' 16 back-to-backs are in a five-way tie for the most in the NBA. They play 22 times in a stretch of three games in four nights, which ranks as the eighth hardest in the league. They are -4 in "net rest" games, which measures who the more tired opponent is in a given game. The Celtics aren't just dealing with the loss of Jaylen Brown this season, they're also needing to navigate one of the league's hardest travel schedules. I still think the Celtics will be a regular season wins machine, and I wouldn't count them out for grabbing the No. 1 seed in the East, but the road to get there looks more daunting after the schedule release.

The Pelicans have the hardest schedule in the NBA this year. New Orleans plays a league-leading 16 back-to-backs, they're the only team in the NBA with 27 'three in four nights' stretches, and they have a -5 net rest disadvantage. The Pelicans already had the league's seventh-lowest over/under at 29.5 wins coming into the season, and it feels like it's going to be an uphill climb to even hit that number. New head coach Jamahl Mosley has his work cut out for him. After years of believing in Zion Williamson, I'm finally giving up the dream that he can be one of the NBA's best players. At this point, I'm more interested in seeing what Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen can do together.

The Bulls are one of the league-leaders with 15 back-to-backs this season. They play a stretch of three games in four nights 24 times, which is the fourth most in the league. They're -3 on "net rest," which is third-hardest in the league. The Bulls also have five time zone crossings on no rest, which is the fifth-most in the league. The first 15 games of the season are especially brutal for Chicago, with two games against Boston, two games against the Knicks, two games against the Sixers, and one game each vs. San Antonio, Minnesota, and Cleveland. The Bulls are starting yet another rebuild, but it's going to be difficult for this fanbase to be patient when the team has the third worst cumulative record in the NBA after the last nine seasons. This year is more about figuring out if they have a future star in Caleb Wilson, and seeing how Matas Buzelis and Josh Giddey develop in their third year together. The Bulls actually have a decent bench led by Leonard Miller, Jalen Smith, and Tre Jones, and they're going to need it with this type of schedule.

The Cavs missed out on LeBron James and got a tough schedule to boot. Cleveland is tied for the league-lead with 16 back-to-backs. They have 23 'three in four nights' games, which is the sixth hardest in the NBA. They're a -2 in rest advantage, also sixth hardest. The Cavs have done a whole lot of nothing this summer coming off the world's least convincing conference finals run, but there's still time to potentially land Peyton Watson or swing a big trade. I just get the sense that Cleveland's Eastern Conference rivals are passing them by … unless Evan Mobley has another leap left in him.

The Mavericks have 16 back-to-backs (tied for the most in the league), and they're at a -3 net rest advantage. It will be fascinating to see how Dallas manages Kyrie Irving as he returns from a torn ACL at age-34. The team will also have to manage Dereck Lively II, because the 22-year-old big man still hasn't been cleared to run after having foot surgery in December. I could see a world where Cooper Flagg takes a big leap and carries the Mavs to playoff contention, but it's important to remember Flagg won't turn 20 years old until just before Christmas. It might be wise for Dallas' new front office to take a more long-term view around their franchise star.

The Lakers play 15 back-to-backs. They face three games in four nights 26 times, which is the second most in the league. There's so much riding on Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves this year. Both of them dealt with injuries last year, playing 115 out of a possible 164 games. That's not going to cut it this year. Doncic and Reaves need to carry this offense every night without LeBron James around, and the Lakers probably don't want to know what happens when Quentin Grimes needs to be their first or second option for a night. Will the Lakers have a plan to save Luka in some back-to-backs? It's going to be a battle in the Western Conference every night, but the Lakers really just need him healthy for the playoffs, unlike last year.

title: Orioles news: O’s back within one game of final wild card spot
description: O’s snap the Rays win streak, a new lineup, and plenty of familiar faces in Tampa.
fullText:
That win felt pretty good! The 6-5 victory over the division-leading Rays, paired with losses by the Tigers, Twins, and Rangers moved the O's to within just one game of the final wild card spot in the American League.

Craig Albernaz deployed a new-look lineup that included Pete Alonso in the lead-off spot, followed by Jackson Holliday and Coby Mayo, while Gunnar Henderson was pushed down to the five hole. It was unconventional, but it's hard to argue with the results. Alonso had two hits, Tyler O'Neill reached based three times as the clean-up hitter, and Henderson led the offense with a 4-for-4 game that included a double, a home run, and two runs scored. His OPS is now .705, the highest it has been since July 4th.

The other headline from this game was the return of Chris Bassitt from the IL. The veteran looked pretty good, batting line through 5.1 innings while giving up two runs on five hits, three walks, and three strikeouts. That's the sort of performance the O's need out of the fifth spot in the rotation, and it's what they weren't getting from Dean Kremer prior to his trade to the Twins.

The only real negative from the game was the ninth inning. That's when Yennier Cano got knocked around and was unable to even finish the frame. He entered with a four-run lead and left after allowing three runs and putting the tying run on second base. Cam Sanders came on the save the day, and he did so with one pitch that Ryan Vilade hit to left field for the final out of the game.

Against all odds, the Orioles find themselves within reach of a wild card spot heading into the final 40 games of the season. Given how poor this team has played at times, that is a minor miracle. It's also a reflection of just how poor the AL is this season.

A win today, along with some helpful results elsewhere, would mean the O's are tied for that final wild card spot by day's end. Kyle Bradish will be on the mound, and we should probably expect a repeat (or similar) of the lineup that Albernaz used on Friday to face the left-handed Ian Seymour. First pitch is 6:10.

Welcome to the Tampa Bay Orioles: 'We just got Orioles 2.0 over here' | The Baltimore Banner
Many of the Rays absolute best players are home grown, but they have certainly done a nice job of filling in some of their key roles on their roster with a few faces that are familiar to the Camden Yards faithful. That feels like something the front office in Baltimore should think about for a while.

The new 'right-handed Schwarber'? Alonso hits leadoff for 1st time | Orioles.com
The Orioles lineup has been stagnant for far too long. They were well past due on a shake up. Is batting Pete Alonso at lead off weird? Absolutely. It's also worth trying to see if it's any better than what they have been running out there for most of the season.

This, that and the other | Roch Kubatko
Plenty of notes about tonight's Rays starter, Seymour, as well as some quote from Albernaz about the lineup construction.

Is it your birthday? Happy birthday!

Jacob Webb turns 33 today. He was a solid reliever for the Orioles between the 2023 and '24 seasons, compiling a 3.09 ERA over 85 total games in those two seasons. The righty has continued to pitch well since departing, first for the Rangers in 2025 and for the Cubs this season.

Chris Singleton is 54 years old. The outfielder spent the 2002 season in Baltimore, when he was worth 1.8 bWAR with a 90 OPS+.

Jeff Huson turns 62. He was a utility option for the Birds during the 1995 and '96 seasons as part of a 12-season MLB career that saw him suit up for seven different clubs.

Tom Dodd is 68 years old. He played in eight MLB games, all of which came with the 1986 Orioles.

1979 – Eddie Murray, normally known for his power rather than speed, steals home in the 12th inning to give the O's and pitcher Mike Flanagan a 2-1 win over the White Sox.

1993 – The Orioles acquired third baseman Mike Pagliarulo from the Twins in exchange for pitcher Erik Schullstrom.

1996 – On their way to an 18-5 win over the Athletics, the Orioles smack five home runs and score 15 times in the final three innings of a game. Chris Hoiles leads the way with two homers while Bobby Bonilla drives in five runs.

2007 – The Orioles cough up a game-tying three-run homer to Shelley Duncan in the bottom of the ninth inning, but rebound in the 10th to score three times against Mariano Rivera for a 6-3 win.

title: Thurman Thomas & 34 Group, Inc. key to Bills’ new Highmark Stadium construction
description: NFL Hall of Fame RB Thurman Thomas, who played 12 seasons for the Buffalo Bills, weighs in about new Highmark Stadium and more.
fullText:
Thurman Thomas is a legend and an icon whose tenacity and grit coupled with truly awe-inspiring traits as a shifty dual-threat running back paved the way for an NFL Hall of Fame career that lasted 12 seasons with the Buffalo Bills. The franchise's Super Bowl teams were perhaps as much defined by Thomas' work as anyone else on the roster.

Teams simply weren't ever quite sure when or where Thomas was going to make them pay, what his next move was from play to play. Keeping up with Thurman Thomas proved far more difficult than anyone had predicted. That proved even more remarkable when years after his retirement Thomas revealed that he played his entire NFL career with a partially torn ACL in his left knee. That's sheer grit and determination, like few others then or now.

At a position with so much franchise star power through various generations, Thomas continues to rise above the rest. He was the complete package on the field then, and he remains so decades after having taken his last handoff in a Bills uniform. For a man who's now spent half his life in Western New York, it might be easy to look back and say he's done it all. Yet, if you ask Thomas, he'd likely tell you he's just getting started.

In a recent conversation with Thurman that set out intent on covering as much ground as was true of his tremendous career, we were drawn to the here and now. For at this moment, something special is unfolding for the whole of Bills Mafia. In case you haven't read the headlines or opened social media in some weeks, One Bills Drive has cut the ribbon on their new home, a completely new, from the ground up, version of Highmark Stadium.

In fact, the franchise just held its first public event for season ticket holders and other lucky fans of the team. In holding its annual "Return of the Blue & Red" practice, the Bills showed more than 50,000 die-hard supporters what all the fuss was about in that giant structure taking shape the last three years across Abbott Road.

Interestingly enough, that's where Thomas' connection here takes shape. While his jersey and number have been retired and adorn the inside of the new Highmark Stadium, that's not his only place of prominence within its walls. Truth be told, Thomas has his name displayed and honored in three separate places inside the new stadium, plus as part of the ring of honor outside the stadium's confines in what's known as the Family Circle.

Yet, the why and where of Thomas' name being included so many places isn't immediately obvious outside of his football career. In speaking with him, the story of a poignant full-circle moment unfolds that finds Thomas continually give back to the community that lifted him on its shoulders.

Thurman and his wife Patti Thomas established 34 Group, Inc. in Buffalo, NY in 2016. As a small business and commercial construction company, 34 Group is a "New York State Certified Minority Business Enterprise (MBE) providing design, construction management and self-performed construction services." Coincidentally, 34 Group was also one of the companies chosen to help with construction of the Bills' new stadium.

Thomas understands the challenges facing any startup, noting the necessary hill climb, and "to be an up-and-coming new group in the Buffalo area, it was a struggle at first." The company wasn't focused on the large prize at first, with Thomas saying "we were confident that we were going to be just a small company — just helping out, really. I mean, because, to have something like a stadium built, we couldn't handle that on our own. And that was Turner and Gilbane [joint venture construction management team Gilbane Building Company and Turner Construction Company] who led the charge for getting everybody set."

Even after this project, Thomas maintains that "we were just the little guys, you know, but we put in all 60 thousand of the seats in the new Highmark Stadium, courtesy of Irwin [Irwin Seating Company]. And they've done an outstanding job with us," while adding that 34 Group also "did some stuff for the grass field."

Focusing exclusively on commercial projects has allowed the Thomases and 34 Group to build a deeper connection with people in Buffalo. Thomas welcomes that bond, saying that it's been really helpful and "gotten me back into the community."

With that community comes projects of all sizes for 34 Group. "Yeah, sure, this was a $2.2 billion job for this stadium, but for our company — we take the $50,000 dollar jobs, we take the $100,000 dollar jobs. Thomas constantly strives to capture something beneficial in any endeavor, stating of a any potential project that "it's that relationship that I always tell my employees that we're not going to win every single job, but make sure you have a relationship, a communication person you can always talk to, because something's always going to pop up."

It's clear Thomas is happy diving into his work with 34 Group, saying that "it's been great, man. I love doing the work around here in the Buffalo area. Thomas maintains that 34 Group is about so much more than the next project. "I mean it's opened so many doors to where — not that we get work — but it's opened so many doors for other things, and I think that's the most important thing, besides our company, is the relationship that we have with the folks in the Buffalo area."

For Thomas, it's perhaps a passion project like no other yet, and one that fate helped connect to his prior career. In asking Thomas about the experience of working alongside other construction outfits and contractors, he said "it's been a really good experience for a lot of the companies in the Buffalo area because I think everybody got a piece of [the action] to do something. I think that was kind of the thing that when we [began building] this stadium — we wanted everybody to get a piece of it. Right? And I think everybody did."

Thomas humbly defers to the expertise and work of the tradespeople within 34 Group. Again, it's a team that undertook the installation of each and every seat — all 60,129 of those red and blue seats — in the new Highmark Stadium. It's an accomplishment he wears proudly upon his sleeve, and something that continues to fuel each and every return trip. "I've been over there probably five or six times in the last couple of weeks and they're still tweaking some things or whatever," Thomas said. A clear sign that despite the already finished look there is still much to do before the regular season is ushered in.

What stands out to him in speaking with folks around town is the sheer magnitude of the project. "From what I'm hearing, a lot of the positives are that people are saying: 'Is this really in Buffalo? Is this type of stadium really in Buffalo?,'" Thomas quipped. "To me, I think it's night and day when you talk about the old Highmark and you talk about the new Highmark. This one here, it's spectacular, there's a lot to see in there and there's a lot of room — a lot of space for the fans to walk around," he added.

Then in a nod to fans' obvious passion for new place, Thomas with a smile on his face said that it was evident during the Blue & Red practice that "everybody wanted to walk around the stadium, right, to see everything — instead of being in their seats." Honestly, who can blame them? Still, it's noteworthy when quarterback Josh Allen is upstaged in any stadium.

With any public project, critiques are bound to catch fire as soon as folks find something to latch onto, either first-hand or from afar. Thomas understands where some fans are coming from in terms of slight-line concerns, but he'd prefer to let the experts handle individual needs, while he focuses on the bigger picture. "It's an outstanding stadium, and I'm so proud that Buffalo does have this," Thomas said emphatically.

As for those seating concerns? Thomas knows it's not unique to Highmark Stadium, stating that "you can go around to all 32 teams in the National Football League, and you're going to have some type of obstructed view or whatever, not a good seat." At the same time, he understands well that people aren't getting the full picture of the situation on social media. "I've been telling people that those seats aren't really made for football. They're made for something else besides, like a concert or something like that," chalking up a lot of the concerns to people taking photos mostly from seats that won't be sold for Bills games.

For Thomas, the here and now is about the new stadium's positive aspects, which extends far beyond the tactile materials. "You know, obviously there's going to be some people out there that don't agree with certain things about the stadium," as nothing on Earth seems to earn unanimous accord simply because there are so many unique perspectives in society. But Thomas isn't ready to concede defeat, in the next breath wondering: "Are those people really fans? Are they really truly fans that are saying 'we're here to watch a football game. We're here to watch our team finally get over the hump to win a Super Bowl. That's all we're here for. I don't care about some obstructed view or anything like that.'"

Thomas continues focusing on the bigger picture, while allowing others to handle the concerns behind the scenes. "I'm sure the Bills and Gilbane and Turner, they'll take care of that situation, they'll do what they need to do in order to move forward. I don't like to hear the negativity talk. I'd like to hear positive talk going forward. We've got a really good football team with a really good chance to win a Super Bowl this year."

It's true that 34 Group is a huge focus for Thomas these days, but it's not his only focus. In a new partnership with Carhartt®, Thomas has found a clothing company that meets the demands of those tradespeople with 34 Group. It's also a company that understands what it means to be hard-working and blue collar. That's something the team has leaned into with its new alternate "Nickel City" uniform in homage to the people of Western New York.

None of that is lost on Thomas, who pointed out how great the new relationship is that he has with Carhartt®. "You know just a couple of years ago they called and wanted to do something with me, with my company at the new stadium. Well of course I don't have any pull over there to get that done so they actually had to call the Buffalo Bills and call the NFL to see if they can someway work something out and it's just one of those things that happened."

Thomas continues to deflect attention, praising the efforts made by both Carhartt® and One Bills Drive. "They worked it out, Carhartt®, you know, had given a lot of money to the community here in Buffalo, which I think they'll continue to do to have that relationship with the Bills, and have that relationship with my company. So, it has turned out great for us, they've been outstanding."

It takes a lot more than large companies to get the work done, however. With a project as grand as Highmark Stadium, that's where an authentically blue-collar attitude pays dividends. Thomas knows that well, especially as it relates to his team and those who have brought the new Highmark to life.

The new home of the Bills really feels like a place built for Buffalo by their neighbors. Thomas points out that the organization got things right in paying tribute to those who helped build a better Highmark. "I think it's on the east side of the stadium, they also have their names on the side of the building for everybody who worked there. It's all about the tradespeople. The ones that really do all the work," Thomas stated.

A dedicated team leader, Thomas understands his role and where he's able to make a positive impact on the team. "I'm not over there doing the work, you know what, but I want to encourage my employees and let everybody know that 'hey, you're doing a great job over here.'"

"It's really the people, the tradespeople that really make this stadium go, that got this stadium built. Without them, we wouldn't be here today. That stadium would not be done," Thomas said. "They've done an outstanding job and it's all about them, it's all about the tradespeople because day in and day out they were over there every single day, no matter what the weather was like, no matter what anything was like they were out there always ready and prepared to go."

These days when discussing the Bills, it seems as though all anyone can talk about is the new stadium. There are a lot of reasons to be excited for the 2026 season, with a new group of coaches in leadership positions, and of course Josh Allen and the rest of the team. However, Highmark Stadium's rebirth is going to demand attention.

The hype is real, and the Blue & Red event was only the tip of the iceberg. Saturday afternoon is the first preseason game on the new grounds, and the players are thrilled to have natural grass waiting for them.

But Saturday is as much about the fans. Even if it's only an exhibition game where the starters may or may not play a meaningful amount of snaps, it's an opportunity for Bills Mafia to test out their lungs.

To help get the crowd pumped, Thomas revealed a giveaway waiting for roughly a third of the first people to enter Highmark. "Saturday, the first 20,000 fans that enter the stadium will get this towel that has every single tradesperson's name on it," a clever rally towel serving as a nod to the hard work that brought the Bills' new home to life.

It will be difficult for anyone entering the new Highmark to forget just how many people were responsible for its development and construction. We've already seen photos of the steel girder adorned by signatures of those involved. There's also a section of wall that lists every person who helped with the stadium's construction, which includes Thomas' name. "Actually, my name is in that building three times," Thomas said. "So… out there on the wall as I said where all the workers (names) were. There's a beam where a lot of the companies signed, and obviously having my jersey retired, my number's in there with Jim and Bruce, and up there with Mr. Wilson also. So, yeah, I'm in there three times," Thomas proudly stated.

As for Saturday afternoon? "Definitely, they'll be pumped," Thomas exclaimed. Bills fans will get two preseason games at home to practice for the regular-season home opener in Week 2. Will waiting until Week 2 stunt the vibe due to a Week 1 road date against the Houston Texans? Thomas isn't convinced that's true, saying "I think, you know, even though with us opening up in Houston on Sunday and they're still playing a game Thursday (Week 2) the fans are like — because it's going to be a tough game in Houston with that defense — but win, lose, or draw, come that Thursday night, the opening of Highmark Stadium, it's going to be electric not only for Bills Mafia and the fans here, but I think when people are watching the game." With the game being in primetime, Thomas is certain that the new stadium's proper opening will resonate with viewers. "I'm sure there'll be some type of highlights where they're showing everybody the stadium, I can guarantee everybody's going to be like 'you know what, that's great for the Buffalo Bills. That's absolutely fantastic.'"

It's fair to say it feels a bit surreal that the stadium is now ready. Thomas summed it up well in saying "it's magical the way it's come together. It's nothing like the other Highmark. It's like, high-tech, red, white, and blue every seat, every place that you go, and it's absolutely gorgeous and I just… I know the people appreciate it." With a new state-of-the-art building for NFL football, you can bet fans will be ready to roar against opposing teams. For his part, Thurman's ready, excited for that moment. "I can't wait to really have it full on Thursday night against the Detroit Lions, you know it's going to be absolutely insane and… man, I'm ready to go. You know, as a Bills fan, you always say 'yeah, this is the year.' Yeah, I definitely think this is the year."

It's natural to guess that Thomas might have an affinity for James Cook, the Bills' current lead running back. Cook has been on an upward trajectory since being drafted 63rd overall by Buffalo during the 2022 NFL Draft. Thomas himself was also a second-round pick of the Bills, going 40th overall in the 1988 NFL Draft. There are plenty of professional similarities that allow them to bond, but their friendship runs far deeper than work parallels.

It's about family, and who Cook is as a person away from the football field. "James' been an outstanding guy. Ever since he got here, you know, we've been really good friends just because — and it's not because, yeah, he plays the position — but I look at his family, I look at his brother Dalvin Cook who I know very very well," Thomas mentioned.

They have a strong connection, Cook and Thomas. "He's such a nice guy; really doesn't say too much, but I think I'm one of those people who can really — I get a lot out of James Cook that anybody else normally wouldn't. So, it's a great relationship."

It's a relationship that allows Thomas to observe Cook's charitable efforts. Thomas knows as well as any former or current Bills player that what you do in the community says as much about you as your on-field effort. With Cook, Thomas sees his efforts as genuine and fruitful. "He's done a great job with the community work that he does," Thomas said.

Being a Buffalo Bill demands more of players than just their in-season work. "You know, you're here throughout the year. You know what? Help out the community," something that Thomas made strides to do as a player and continues doing now later in life. As for Cook's work in that realm? "He's done an excellent job. Really, that whole organization, all those player have done an excellent job of being in the community and doing things for Bills Mafia and people around there."

Many Bills fans have called for Cook to get more opportunities as a receiver, something Thomas did well during his career. Thomas agrees, and says that "hopefully that'll be coming," while revealing "I talked to him like, 'yeah, you know what, with your ability, and your speed, and your quickness, man, I really would like to see a little bit more out of you in the passing game.

There's more to Cook developing further as a receiver than just having plays called for him. He needs to continue working toward a full-time role where sometimes he isn't the focal point as a blocker instead, which Thomas isn't shy to point out. "In order for him to do that, he has to be out on the football field first, second, and third down. So, I don't know how much that's going to come into the offense, but I think he's ready to go and have an even better year this year."

While chatting with Thomas at the new stadium, Cook revealed that his personal goals this coming season are to try and win the NFL rushing title again, and to rush for 2,000 yards in the process. Of course, top of mind is his quest to help bring the Lombardi Trophy home to Orchard Park, NY next February.

Thurman Thomas continues to lead by example as an inspirational person who works to improve his community and help lift others up. Much of that is due to Patti and Thurman's charitable efforts, but also because they decided to invest in building Buffalo better.

In many ways, the new Highmark Stadium is a fitting tribute to the work done by so many Western New Yorkers on a daily basis. That includes those lofty heights Thomas, his teammates and coaches continually battled back against in pursuit of Super Bowl Glory.

At the end of the season, Thomas may be right in saying that this really is the Bills' year. Should that play out as true, then he and 34 Group, Inc. will have played a part in bringing Bills Mafia a whole new level of energy and life at home. It all has the feel of a story 30 years in the making.

title: Yankees Rivalry Roundup: Rays and Red Sox both take losses
description: The Yankees lost on Friday, but it didn’t cost them ground in the standings.
fullText:
The Yankees traveled north of the border on Friday, as they opened up a series against the Blue Jays. However, they left their bats — or whatever is left of them — back in the states. The lineup mustered just one run as they dropped the opener 3-1 to Toronto.

While the Yankees stunk up the joint yesterday, did anyone give them a helping hand in the various playoff races. Let's check in today's edition of the Rivalry Roundup.

The Rays very nearly climbed all the way out of a four-run hole in the ninth inning, but they fell one short, stranding the potential game-tying run at second as the Orioles finished things off behind Cam Sanders, snapping Tampa Bay's nine-game winning streak.

The two teams traded off runs in the second and third innings, with the O's taking 1-0 and 2-1 leads, only for the game to be tied by Tampa Bay shortly after. The game stayed tied for a while after that, as Chris Bassitt put in a solid effort for Baltimore fresh off the 60-day IL, matched by a combined effort by the Rays' bullpen.

The deadlock was broken when Dylan Beavers drove home two runs on a single in the seventh inning. Amid a deeply disappointing season, Gunnar Henderson then gave Baltimore some breathing room when he hit a two-run homer in the eighth. That seemed like it would be plenty enough, but it very nearly wasn't.

Tampa Bay started the bottom of the ninth with two singles and a wild pitch moving two runners into scoring position. Jonathan Aranda cashed in on that opportunity, driving home two runs with a single. A walk and a pair of stolen bases then put the tying run in scoring position, but Junior Caminero managed just a run-scoring ground out. Baltimore opted to issue an intentional walk Liam Hicks, which did put the winning run on base, but the gambit worked and the O's escaped and eked out the win. The Rays remain 6.5 games ahead of the Yankees and the O's got to within a game of the Tigers and Rangers for the last Wild Card spot — though the Twins and Blue Jays also sit between them.

Pittsburgh Pirates (60-64) 8, Boston Red Sox (65-57) 4: The Pirates got to Red Sox pitching to the tune of two home runs and eight runs in total, keeping Boston from gaining ground on the Yankees. Former Yankee prospect Rafael Flores Jr. got Pittsburgh on the board in the second, and the Bucs then scored a combined six runs over the fourth and fifth to fully take control of the game. In terms of pure numbers, the Red Sox actually recorded the same number of hits as Pittsburgh with nine, but the Pirates just did far more damage with their chances.

Chicago White Sox (63-58) 9, Detroit Tigers (60-62) 5: Miguel Vargas went 4-for-5 with two home runs and three RBI to lead the White Sox past the Tigers. Chicago took control of this game with a five-run fourth inning, which included a Munetaka Murakami homer and a two-run Braden Montgomery triple. The White Sox didn't have a particularly sterling pitching day, they just never remotely needed one; now, they're 3.5 games ahead of Detroit in the AL Central.

Houston Astros (63-60) 10, Seattle Mariners (57-66) 7 – 10 innings: An absolutely wild 10th inning saw the Astros give up two runs in the top of the frame before scoring five in the bottom of it to walk off with the win. Houston led for most of the game before the M's scored two in the eighth to tie things up and eventually send it to extras. Seattle then seemingly took control in the 10th, with a Victor Robles' triple leading the way to them putting up two runs. However, they couldn't hold that edge, and Christian Walker eventually sent everyone home with a three-run homer. Houston is 2.5 games ahead of Texas in the AL West, while the M's continue to fade (six back of Houston and 3.5 behind the Wild Card).

fullText:
The UFC is at Philadelphia's Xfinity Mobile Arena for tonight's UFC 330 fight card. The Paramount+ streaming event finds two UFC belts up for grabs at the top of the card. In the main event, UFC welterweight champion Islam Makhachev faces Ian Machado Garry. Also on the line, Makhachev's UFC record tying 16-fight winning streak. Meanwhile, in the evening's co-main event, Mackenzie Dern looks to defend her strawweight line against Gillian Robertson.

UFC Announces Full 13-Fight Card For UFC 331

Date: Saturday, August 15, 2026

Main Card Start Time: 9:00 p.m. ET

Preliminary Card Start Time: 7:00 p.m. ET

Early Prelims Start Time: 5:30 p.m. ET

Location: Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia, PA

Islam Makhachev vs. Ian Machado Garry

Mackenzie Dern vs. Gillian Robertson

Mansur Abdul-Malik vs. Dustin Stoltzfus

Edson Barboza vs. Esteban Ribovics

Chidi Njokuani vs. Joel Álvarez

Charles Johnson vs. Eduardo Chapolin

Donte Johnson vs. Eric McConico

Rafael Tobias vs. Lucas Fernando

Jeremiah Wells vs. Myktybek Orolbai

UFC Announces Six Bouts For 2026 Noche UFC Fight Card

Islam Makhachev (28-1) was 11-0 when he joined the UFC in 2015. He won his promotional debut, submitting Leo Kuntz in the second round. In his second scrap under the UFC banner, Adriano Martins knocked out Makhachev in the first round. That loss remains the only blemish on the record of the now 32-year-old Makhachev.

After the loss to Martins, Makhachev ran off 10 straight wins. That run earned him the No. 4 spot in the UFC lightweight rankings and set him up to face ex-champ Charles Oliveira in a battle for the vacant lightweight crown. Makhachev claimed the belt with a second-round submission win in 2022.

In his first two title defenses, Makhachev faced then-UFC featherweight champ Alexander Volkanovski. He won the first bout at UFC 284 by decision and followed that with a knockout win over Volkanovski at UFC 294.

In June 2024, the UFC matched Makhachev against former interim UFC lightweight titleholder Dustin Poirier. Makhachev submitted Poirier in the fifth round of that contest, which headlined UFC 302.

In January 2025, Makhachev defended his crown with a quick submission win over late replacement Renato Moicano, who stepped in to replace Arman Tsarukyan on weigh-in day. The victory gave Makhachev the record for most consecutive UFC lightweight title defenses at four.

After that victory, Makhachev moved up to welterweight, surrendering his 155-pound title. In his first bout at 170 pounds, Makhachev cruised to a decision win over Jack Della Maddalena at UFC 322 in November 2025, easily wresting the UFC welterweight crown from Della Maddalena.

With that win, Makhachev tied the record for longest winning streak in UFC history. He is tied with Anderson Silva for that record.

Ian Machado Garry (17-1) has an 10-1 record under the UFC banner. The 28-year-old has seven decisions and three knockouts. In June 2024, Machado Garry defeated Michael "Venom" Page at UFC 303 to earn his eighth straight winunder the UFC banner. However, he tasted defeat in his next outing, dropping a decision to Shavkat Rakhmonov at UFC 310.

Machado Garry initially came across as a Conor McGregor clone, but the confident Irish fighter has found his own personality as a competitor who is more than willing to take on the toughest the competitors the UFC can book him against, something he did again in accepting a short notice fight against the dangerous Carlos Prates in April 2025. Machado Garry won that five-round bout via decision.

In his most recent outing, Machado Garry bested former UFC welterweight champion Belal Muhammad in November.

Machado Garry is the No. 2 UFC welterweight in the new Meta rankings.
